conviction_note: The findings sum to -1.3 and the scaled number is -0.52 (p_up 46 x abs 6.5). The negatives are the closest peer's post-quarter print (Futu Q3: volume -22% q/q, revenue -7.1% q/q) and a weak HKEX turnover exit into Q4. Both set a revenue bar of about $174-177M, which implies only -3 to -5% q/q, against a likely revenue of $168-174M. The offsets are a tax-rate normalisation, record Q3 HK equity issuance for the underwriting line, and a beaten-down stock. The stock is near its 52-week low, about 20% off since the last print, with call-heavy open interest, and the peer itself rose +2.8% on a weak-quarter revenue beat. Those offsets keep p_up close to 50. The panel should read this as a mild lean on proxies, not a document-level call.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $174-177M. Yahoo analysis shows $174.1M from 1 analyst (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TIGR/analysis, read 2026-11-23); Chartmill shows $177.25M as relayed in a search snippet, with a mis-dated report date (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/TIGR/estimates, 403 on fetch). The two roughly agree. Year-ago revenue was $175.2M and Q2 2026 was $182.3M. The non-GAAP EPS bar is disputed: Benzinga shows $0.21 (possibly stale, updated 2026-10-30, https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/TIGR/earnings-forecasts) and Chartmill $0.28. Q2 2026 non-GAAP EPS was $0.23. There is no company revenue guidance, only operating commentary (Q3 volume and commissions 'slightly below' Q2 at 2026-08-26; new funded accounts flat or higher; CAC $450-550; tax rate 10-15%). Revenue-dependent findings are capped small because the bar rests on 1-2 thin estimates.
positioning_check: Short interest 8.61M shares, days to cover 3.9 (shortsqueeze.com page dated 2026-11-23, https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=TIGR). Another snippet shows 9.1M shares, 5.2 DTC at the 2026-09-30 settlement (curvedtrading.com). On roughly 170-180M ADS-equivalents that is about 5% of float, so the short is not crowded. Skew_25d +3.37 vol points: downside modestly paid. Put/call OI 0.22, so open interest is call-heavy. ATM spread is 28.6% of mid. Event-implied move 5.62%, straddle 7.8%. Tape: -4.4% over 20 days, -3.0% over 5 days, -64.8% from the 52-week high, +10% off the 52-week low. The shares are down about 20% since the Q2 print (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-16). 11 brokers, 10 buy/overweight, mean target $7.71 (Longbridge, 2026-10-17).

findings.finding: Futu, the closest peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-19, after TIGR last spoke (2026-08-26). Its total trading volume was HK$5.01T, -22.0% q/q (US stocks -24.0% q/q, HK stocks -19.2% q/q). Total revenue was -7.1% q/q, client assets -4.6% q/q ('lower market valuations') and the margin balance -22.3% q/q. Applying Futu's -7% q/q to TIGR's $182.3M Q2 gives about $169.5M. The $174-177M bar implies only -3% to -4.5% q/q, so TIGR revenue is more likely at or below the bar than above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 revenue of $175.2M beat a ~$132.8M estimate by a wide margin and the stock traded about +9% premarket (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/why-tigr-stock-rose-premarket-trade-today/cLILDuARESm). The record Q2 2026 revenue was sold: -0.1% close per FX News, -7.3% per Simply Wall St (https://fxnewsgroup.com/forex-news/retail-forex/tiger-brokers-shares-flat-despite-record-q2-2026-revenues-of-160-7m/). Q1 2026 traded -3.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: TIGR has a single visible revenue estimate ($174.1M, 1 analyst on Yahoo), which looks unrevised for a peer print that landed five days ago. If the market had priced Futu's q/q drop into TIGR, the estimate would sit near $165-170M. The offset: Futu itself beat its own consensus by 11% (HK$6.69B vs HK$6.03B) and rose +2.8%, so peer consensus was cut and TIGR's may be stale-high rather than stale-low.
findings.independence: HKEX Q3 cash ADT -12% q/q (finding 2, a different source: https://www.chinadailyhk.com/article/642355). TIGR management's own 2026-08-26 comment that volume and commissions were 'slightly below' Q2 points the same way, softer (https://www.webull.com/news/15497781686772736). Futu's revenue beat against its own bar points the other way (https://finviz.com/news/425248/futu-holdings-shares-rise-28-as-third-quarter-revenue-beats-estimates-despite-earnings-miss).

findings.finding: Hong Kong cash turnover weakened through Q3 and into Q4. HKEX Q3 2026 ADT fell 12% q/q and 11% y/y. Monthly ADT was HK$201.9B in September and HK$180.7B in October, against a 9-month average of HK$272.9B. IBKR's October 2026 client equity fell 4% m/m and DARTs were -4% y/y. So any October/November quarter-to-date commentary on the 8:00 ET call is likely to read soft for trading volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TIGR gives no formal guidance; QTD commentary is the forward line. At Q2 (2026-08-26) a 'slightly below Q2' QTD comment came with a flat to -7% close (sources conflict).
findings.why_not_priced: These are public macro series, so partly priced: the stock is near its 52-week low and down about 20% since the last print. What would be visible if fully priced is a TIGR revenue estimate that already embeds a down Q4; the single estimate for Q4 EPS ($0.15 on Benzinga) does embed some decline, which cuts this finding's size.
findings.independence: IBKR October 2026 metrics, a different source (https://finviz.com/news/413393/interactive-brokers-group-reports-brokerage-metrics-and-other-financial-information-for-october-2026-includes-reg-nms-execution-statistics). IBKR's October DARTs rose 5% m/m, which partly offsets. The HKEX monthly figures come from the same reporting as finding 1's HK leg, but not from the Futu document.

findings.finding: On the 2026-08-26 call management said Q3-to-date client assets were up a high single digit q/q, with net inflows and mark-to-market each above $1B. It expected new funded accounts flat or higher vs Q2's 32.6K, net inflow per new user about $25K, and 'some recovery' in the cash-equity take rate from Q2's 3.6bps. It also said mainland outflows had 'largely run its course'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026's record $2.9B net inflow came with a -3.9% reaction, because the penalty dominated. Account and asset metrics have not driven positive reactions in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced: it is the company's own public commentary and lands inside what was guided. A small positive remains because Futu's -4.6% q/q client assets suggest a September give-back; if TIGR's assets still print up q/q, that is better than the peer.
findings.independence: Futu's Q3 funded-account net adds of about 163K (173K excluding mainland China and Japan) show the account-growth channel still working across the sector (https://finviz.com/news/424998/futu-announces-third-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results).

findings.finding: Q2 2026's effective tax rate was about 28%, inflated by treating the $59.7M CSRC penalty as nondeductible (about +$6M of tax). Management guided a normalised 10-15% and said it would gradually reverse the penalty tax effect against H2 tax expense. That lifts Q3 net income per dollar of pretax profit by roughly 15-20% vs Q2, which cushions EPS against the $0.21-0.28 bar even if revenue slips.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to a tax line at TIGR. Below-the-line items are sized at a fraction of operating profit.
findings.why_not_priced: It is guided, so mostly in the models. The EPS estimates disagree ($0.21 vs $0.28), and a model still carrying the 28% rate would be visibly low.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview restates the 10-15% expectation (https://finviz.com/news/423387/up-fintechs-post-penalty-rebound-faces-a-take-rate-and-account-growth-test-as-shares-slide). It shares the same company commentary as its source, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: Hong Kong equity issuance set records in Q3 2026: a record US$47.5B of Q3 share sales, and nine-month IPO proceeds above HK$388B, a record per KPMG. TIGR's 'other revenues' line was $21.0M in Q2, +67.6% y/y, with 14 HK IPOs underwritten and $26.3M in Q3 2025. That line is likely flat to up q/q while commissions fall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate reaction history. The line is about 12% of revenue, so its effect is net of the commission decline in finding 1.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy and the wire previews do not mention it; the Earnings Whispers preview focuses on take rate and accounts. If priced, it would show as an estimate above the volume-implied number, and the $174-177M bar may already partly reflect it.
findings.independence: Q3 share-sale record reported separately (https://aiweekly.co/alerts/hong-kong-hits-record-475b-q3-share-sale-haul-as-ai-deal-frenzy-drives-ipos-and). TIGR has not confirmed its Q3 underwriting count, so this is a proxy.

findings.finding: Costs are rising into falling revenue. Q2 total operating costs were $103.9M, +46.5% y/y: marketing +86.6%, communication and market data +56.4%, G&A +44.6%. H2 CAC is guided up to $450-550 from about $450, and new funded accounts are guided flat or higher. With Q3 net revenue likely below Q2's $160.7M, operating margin should compress from Q2's 35% (op income $56.8M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 was sold -7.3% per AllInvestView/Simply Wall St on margin compression from a lower take rate (https://fxnewsgroup.com/forex-news/retail-forex/tiger-brokers-shares-flat-despite-record-q2-2026-revenues-of-160-7m/ reports the flat version).
findings.why_not_priced: The cost guide is public. What is not visible is how far revenue falls under a near-fixed cost base. Q2's severance was one-time and may come out, which partly offsets.
findings.independence: The CAC guide comes from the call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15497781686772736). It shares the company's own disclosure, so it is not fully independent of finding 3.

findings.finding: Positioning is set up for relief rather than for a further leg down. TIGR is at $3.91, +10% off its 52-week low and -64.8% from its high, and down about 20% since the Q2 print while the S&P barely moved. Short interest is modest (about 5% of float, 3.9 DTC) and option open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.22). The closest peer rose +2.8% on 2026-11-19 on a weak-quarter revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In 2026 the stock has not rallied on prints (Q1 -3.9%, Q2 flat to -7%), so 'cheap' has not paid on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Skew is only +3.37 vol points, so downside protection is modestly bid and the options are not pricing a large relief move. A low-bar setup would show as call skew or a positive run-up, and neither is present.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview on the 20% slide since the last report and the $50M buyback with only about $5M used (https://finviz.com/news/423387/up-fintechs-post-penalty-rebound-faces-a-take-rate-and-account-growth-test-as-shares-slide). Short data from https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=TIGR.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter under the mainland liquidation-only regime: no new positions or deposits for mainland users from 2026-06-12. Mainland revenue contribution had already fallen to 15-20% in Q2 from 20-25%, and mainland users held under 10% of client assets. Revenue from that cohort should decline further in Q3, and the call will likely disclose a lower share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The penalty announcement was -28 to -32% on 2026-05-22. The Q2 disclosure of the 15-20% share came with a flat to -7% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the wind-down is public and management called the outflows largely over. This item stays negative only because the reported quarter carries the full-quarter drag, which models may underweight.

findings.finding: Management reaffirmed a 150K new-funded-account target for 2026. With 61.5K added in H1, it needs about 44K a quarter in H2, against 32.6K in Q2 and a Q3 guide of 'flat or higher' vs Q2. A Q3 print in the mid-30Ks would push the full-year target toward a trim on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to an account-target change at TIGR.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public (an Earnings Whispers preview spells it out), so this is mostly priced. The residual is the guide change itself, if it comes.
findings.independence: The Q3 'flat or higher' guide comes from the call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15497781686772736). It is a different document but the same company statement.

baseline_tension: The mild negative lean agrees with the modest put skew (+3.37) and the negative run-up, so it is partly priced. The positioning finding cuts against both, which is why p_up sits at 46 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs): the tax-normalisation and penalty-tax-reversal finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.2 because it sits below operating income.
Rule 7 and the skew: the HKEX/IBKR macro finding agrees with the put skew and is a public series, so it was shrunk from -0.8 to -0.6.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the funded-account target finding was cut from -0.4 to -0.3, because the Q3 'flat or higher' guide already tells the market about 44K a quarter is a stretch.

Left standing: the Futu peer finding at -1.0. 'A peer's print landing after the company last spoke' is a pattern this file says has paid; it is kept small because the bar rests on 1-2 thin estimates (rule 6 cap).
abs_move_pct 6.5 and p_up 46 unchanged: rule 8 and the core's understatement warning argue against shrinking abs_move below the 5.6% implied move.
